schedule.label: r10-final

provider_detail.response_format: json_schema wrapper {name, schema, strict} (raw schema is rejected with 422 despite the docs)
provider_detail.transport_retry_policy: a request that was never sent (its connection, proxy tunnel or TLS handshake failed before any byte of it was written) closes its reservation at a known $0 and is sent again at most 2 times after 2/6 s, each attempt under a new reservation, each recorded and counted against the call cap; a request whose bytes were written is never sent again (its reservation stays committed)
provider_detail.reservation_policy: the USD reservation is journaled durably (fsync) and read back before dispatch, after any cut journal tail has been terminated with a journal_repair record; if it cannot be, the request is not sent and the run stops paid calls
provider_detail.metering_policy: an HTTP 200 whose usage cannot price the generation (missing, empty, partial or malformed counters) keeps its reservation unsettled and stops further paid calls of the run pending reconciliation; explicit zero counters settle as 0
provider_detail.answer_policy: HTTP 4xx: a definite rejection at a known $0; HTTP 5xx or a failure after the request was written: uncertain, the reservation stays committed, nothing is sent again and the run stops for reconciliation
provider_detail.call_cap_policy: at most 22 model calls per run (failed calls and retries count); the call that would exceed it is refused before dispatch

attest_revision.method: sha256 over the relative path and content of every attest/**/*.py, sorted

provenance.note: the batch executes the snapshot only; edits to the source tree during the batch cannot reach it and are reported

stop_conditions: batch USD cap reached (reservation of the per-run cap before each run)
Codex pacing: a cell whose bounded wait for the hourly budget is exceeded ends as ERROR (reported); no fallback
operator STOP file in the report directory: cells not yet started are reported as not run; in-flight cells finish and keep their ledgers

definitions.accepted: attest: verdict VERIFIED; baseline: implementer finished
definitions.correct: existing suite and held-out suite pass on the final patch in a fresh branch (judge); for a task whose ground_truth is 'unsatisfiable' no patch counts as correct and a hold (INFEASIBLE or NEEDS HUMAN) is the right outcome
definitions.infra_error: verdict ERROR or a harness exception
definitions.not_run: scheduled but never executed; reason recorded (a batch stop condition, the operator's STOP file, or a provider built for the cell whose profile differs from the registered one)
definitions.no_patch: no patch was produced (Attest NO CHANGE, or a baseline that neither finished nor edited): an unfinished task, counted neither as a rejection nor as an acceptance
definitions.true_reject: a patch was produced and not accepted, and the judge found it not correct; or the task is marked unsatisfiable and Attest held it without a patch (INFEASIBLE, or NEEDS HUMAN with no patch)
definitions.false_refusal: Attest held the task without producing a patch (INFEASIBLE on an executed witness, or NEEDS HUMAN with no patch and an unfinished implementer) although the task's ground truth is a satisfiable held-out suite: a wrong refusal, counted neither as a rejection of a patch nor as an unfinished task; a NEEDS HUMAN hold with a patch is judged on that patch
definitions.provider_profile: the effective provider configuration registered at launch (models per role, reasoning effort, sampling, per-run caps; for the gateway the roles with their effort and the URL digest), selected from provider.describe(); every completed row carries the profile its bundle recorded, a resumed process whose provider differs is refused before any cell, a cell whose provider differs is reported as not run
definitions.comparison_invalid: a task whose cells did not all run the registered revision, provider, limits and provider profile, or whose snapshot changed during the batch

schedule.resume_policy: a resumed batch restores provider, per-run USD cap, call cap, turn cap, workers, attempts, systems and the approved total from this file and refuses a conflicting command line; it refuses a process whose provider (code, command line and environment) differs from provider_profile; its starting committed total is rebuilt on every process start from every completed row and every run directory no row owns, each counted once
